walkthroughs.body_html:
Solar System Dynamics — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Solar System Dynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Solar System Dynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Length of the solar cycle (sunspot count)?
options: 1 year
11 years
22 years
50 years

mcqs.q: Charged particles streaming from the Sun are called?
options: Solar flares
Solar wind
Aurora
Cosmic rays

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: It is made of fire.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
By measuring its colour with the naked eye.

mcqs.q: How do astronomers determine the chemical composition of a distant star?
options: It is made of fire.
By sending probes to collect samples.
By measuring its colour with the naked eye.
By analysing absorption lines in its spectrum.

mcqs.q: What is a black hole's event horizon?
options: The boundary beyond which not even light can escape.
A literal horizon you can walk to.
By measuring its colour with the naked eye.
The visible 'edge' of the black hole.
